_about: How big a party is (rule 75b: 'a party is sized by Battle Brothers' math, never twelve against twelve, and the first roads give a few thugs'). The INPUTS and their directions are Battle Brothers' (the wiki's Game Mechanics page and GROK_60): roster strength, the job's skulls, days, distance from towns, the combat difficulty, the count words. The wiki gives NO arithmetic from those to a head count, and no unit costs, so the few coefficients that make a number are OURS, draft, each marked 'ours', calibrated on the rule's own anchor (a fresh three-man crew's first job on day one is a few thugs) and waiting on Grok ask 22 (the hidden formulas) and TUNING. The MAKE-UP of a party (thugs, raiders, a leader) is COMBAT's, by tier, in ours.json enemy_tiers; this file only says how many.

roster_strength.quote: the strength of your roster (which equals a sum of individual strengths [10 + 2*(lvl-1)] of 12 strongest brothers) / (GROK_60) Peasant militia and manhunters use 14

day_cap.quote: A roaming party uses days and the crew score. Day scaling for those stops at day 100.

difficulty_by_pick.quote: Combat difficulty which is set at the start of the game, which increases both numbers and tier / COMBAT's scale (ours.json enemy_tiers): 0 Beginner, 1 Veteran, 2 Expert, 3 Legendary; each above Veteran counts as 20 days later

NEW HERE keeps Beginner's aim and the slower dress (job_bb.dress_ahead 2.5); SEEN IT is the math; OUTLIVED IT keeps its 15% more, Battle Brothers' Expert step as its modders name it (rule 380: closeness_bands.steps, the gate's leg D1).

job_bb.source: reference/library/grok/GROK_ASK_105_KEYBOARD_CONTRACTS_SCALING_2026_10_24.md (Grok, unverified, PASSED FILTER 10/25; the wiki's Game Mechanics page agrees on the inputs): k, exp, mult_min, mult_max are Battle Brothers'; base_men and dress are OURS (WORLD [most jobs fit the company], rule 192, 10/25), calibrated on the live fight by tools/bohemia_world_most_jobs_fit.js
job_bb.quote: The final multiplier is 94 percent times (1 percent times roster strength) raised to the power of 0.89. The multiplier cannot be lower than 0.75 or higher than 5. / Non-contract locations and most roaming parties scale mainly with days and distance to civilization.
job_bb.why: Rule 192 (Paolo 10/25: 'why is the game so in love with throwing overpowered enemies in like 75% of the quests I take... look how Battle Brothers does it'). MEASURED on the live fight before: a job's count grew one for one with his men and their levels (job.strength_per_enemy) AND its enemies were dressed by the calendar day, so a day-20 company of six at level 3 met 7 to 11 men dressed for day 20: a one-skull job won 33 in 100, three skulls 13, an enemy OUTCLASSED him in 97 to 100 fights. Battle Brothers scales a contract by the company's strength alone, bent down (^0.89) and floored (0.75), and only roaming parties by the days. NOW a job's count is base_men[skulls] x that multiplier x the difficulty, and it is DRESSED for the day a typical company stands that strong (dress: [strength, day], the company of tools/bohemia_world_most_jobs_fit.js: day 1 a new crew of three, day 20 six at level 3, day 50 nine at 5, day 90 twelve at 8). Calibrated (30 fights a cell): one skull won 90 to 100 at every point, two 70 to 80, three 50 to 80 (a real risk, the stars say so); a crew of three at day 6 and 30: 97, 67 to 73, 30 to 37. AMENDED 10/26 (EYES round three: the Block Watch's twelve at level 1 met an LV 8 Marauder with 386 armour on days one and two): the dress day is never later than the calendar's day (BOHEMIA_CITY_WORLD.html __NO_CHAMPION_ON_DAY_ONE__): Battle Brothers grows a contract's count with the company and its kinds with the days, so a strong crew early meets more men of the early kinds.
job_bb.dress_ahead_why: DIFFICULTY [the curve] 11/3 (rule 351(d), ask line 363; Paolo 11/3: 'day 20 with like 10 super soldiers... I reached the ceiling'). MEASURED before (tools/bohemia_difficulty_the_curve.js, banks/BOHEMIA_DIFFICULTY_THE_CURVE_BEFORE_11_3_26.json): the dress never ran past the calendar, so a company standing at day-57 strength on day 20 met day-20 men, and every level won the day's hardest job 90 to 100 in 100 from day 13 to day 30. NOW, after the first week (from_day, rule 120(a)'s thugs first), each day counts mult days by level (NEW HERE 2.5, SEEN IT 3, OUTLIVED IT 4), never past the day the company's own strength stands for (dress): a weak company still meets the easy dress, a strong one meets the late kinds about day 29, 25 and 19. OURS (draft), calibrated on the live fight; the direction is Battle Brothers' ('harder enemy groups appear sooner' on a higher combat difficulty, bb_all/0828:16; a contract 'closely matched to the player's party', :109).
job_bb.dress_ahead_amended_11_3: TUNING 2 [the fight is close] 11/3 (VAMILY rule 370, ask line 396; records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_FIGHT_IS_CLOSE_11_3_26.md): SEEN IT's calendar counts 3.5 days a day after the first week (was 3) and OUTLIVED IT's 4.5 (was 4); NEW HERE's stays 2.5. A strong company meets the late men (dress day 60) about day 28 on NEW HERE, 22 on SEEN IT, 18 on OUTLIVED IT (it was 28, 25, 20); never past the day the company's own strength stands for, so a weak one meets the early men on every level. This keeps the three levels apart now that NEW HERE fields the full crew (difficulty_count_mult).

closeness_bands.source: VAMILY.md rule 370 (Paolo 11/3) and 351(c); records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_THE_FIGHT_IS_CLOSE_AND_STILL_FEELS_GOOD_11_3_26.md; measured by tools/bohemia_difficulty_the_curve.js --close (banks/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_FIGHT_IS_CLOSE_BEFORE_11_3_26.json, _AFTER_); Battle Brothers' floor: banks/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_WHOLE_GRID_10_18_26.json setting 'bb' (Battle Brothers' Veteran on our fight: twelve men against the map's thirteen won 95 to 99 in 100 with 1.2 to 2.8 men struck down a fight and nobody down in only 12 to 33 fights of 100)
closeness_bands.quote: for all difficulties the tuning is so important, the numbers, how close things can get, but you still feel good
closeness_bands.why: TUNING 2 [the fight is close] 11/3: THE BANDS gates/the_fight_is_close_gate.js holds, per level, on the routine job and the tough job (one skull and two to day 3, then two and three), pooled over the Lone Wolf, a fresh company and his way (rare men in the cheapest kit) at sample_days: won in 100, men struck down a fight, fights in 100 where nobody of his went under half health (clean_at_most), the company's health left at the end (hp_at_most), and the share of the enemy's landed hits that took half a man or more (big_at_least). Battle Brothers' Veteran on our own fight (10/18) is the floor the two harder levels sit on; NEW HERE is Battle Brothers' Beginner (rule 370(1): even the easiest bites). not_hell: OUTLIVED IT's routine job on not_hell_days is won at least this often by every company, the Lone Wolf alone included (351(c)). price_ladder: the dearest body and helmet cost at least this many times the cheapest piece holding a third as much (Battle Brothers' curve is about 30 to 50; kept). one_shot: an unarmoured man's health and a mail shirt's armour for the one-shot leg (a 60-health recruit, Battle Brothers' mail hauberk 150).
closeness_bands.seen_tough_why: Set where the live fight stands after COMBAT 7's rule 366 (the enemy that wants to live breaks and runs) landed in the same hour: SEEN IT's tough job at days 10 and 20 went from 94 to 97 in 100 won and 1.25 to 0.95 men down a fight on main's own numbers; the band was 96 and 1.0. Tightening it back needs the brigand levers WORLD's gate pins (records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_FIGHT_IS_CLOSE_11_3_26.md s7): TUNING's next round.
closeness_bands.big_beasts_why: TUNING 2 11/3, rule 370(9) (Paolo: 'these big ass animals better fuck you up if they get close to you for real'): the big beasts are deadly up close. O2: each kind's blow at its best takes half an unarmoured man (one_shot.health) and the four heavy ones (through_mail) half a man in mail (one_shot.mail_body) too; the cat's bite stays a cat's (a cougar's teeth do not go through mail; its danger is the ambush and the pin). B5: in fights against them (the curve tool --factions, the three companies at days, every level), at least big_share_at_least in 100 of their landed blows take half a man, and armoured_big_share_at_least in 100 even on the Lone Wolf's company in the shop's armour. MEASURED: 17 and 1 before (the unhold's Sweep, 40-80, held to a tenth of a man by mail), 48 and 15 after (banks/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_BIG_BEASTS_BEFORE/AFTER_11_3_26.json); the fights are still won 97 to 100 in 100, because they are shot on the way in.
closeness_bands.steps_why: TUNING 2 11/3, rule 380 (Paolo: 'Battle Brothers from easy to hard just tweaked the numbers tiny, so slightly, to make it harder'): THE LEVELS ARE SMALL STEPS. count_step: no level's crew (difficulty_count_mult) is more than this from its neighbour, and SEEN IT is the math itself (1): Battle Brothers' Expert step as its modders name it, 1.15 (records/BOHEMIA_DIFFICULTY_ROUND_1_THE_CURVE_11_3_26.md s3, 'from 1.15 to 1.5'). aim_step: no level's hit shift (ours.json hit_roll_shift) is more than Battle Brothers' own Beginner step from its neighbour, 5 points each way (bb_all/0828_Game Mechanics.txt). And no easier level is harder than the next on any lever: crews, aim, how soon the late men come (job_bb.dress_ahead) and the tier's days (ours.json enemy_tiers.difficulty_days). records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_DIFFICULTY_FINE_TUNED_11_3_26.md.

job_contract.source: JOBS [jobs that fit] 11/8 (VAMILY rule 436(c), asks 102 and 114): Battle Brothers' contract is ONE budget spent on the enemy's own cost (reference/library/grok/wiki/PAGES_ALL.tar.gz bb_all/0827_Game Guide.txt: the contract's type base value 'is multiplied by the other variables'; 'The maximum number and type of enemies is limited by the spawn list used'), sized off the roster (levels, never gear: bb_all/0828_Game Mechanics.txt). The numbers are OURS, measured on the live fight by tools/bohemia_jobs_beast_cost.js (a new crew of three at level 2 in its own kit, AUTO both sides, 16 plays a cell, dress day 5): brigands 4 / 5 / 6 at 0.85 / 0.71 / 0.61 of the AUTO count; dire wolves 2 / 3 / 4 at 0.91 / 0.46 / 0.08; hyenas 2 / 3 / 4 at 0.96 / 0.74 / 0.16; war dogs as men (1.11, not costed); coyotes weaker than men (1.62, the fight's own 1.0 stands). TUNING's one table section Y holds every row.
job_contract.quote: Each type of contract has a base value that ranges from 40 to 200. It's multiplied by the other variables. / The maximum number and type of enemies is limited by the spawn list used (the difficulty doesn't scale indefinitely). / From further testing, gear does not appear to have an impact on roster strength.
job_contract.why: Rule 436(c) and 192 (Paolo: 'why is the game so in love with throwing overpowered enemies in like 75% of the quests I take... look how Battle Brothers does it'). MEASURED on the demo before (tools/bohemia_jobs_fit_the_company.js, 20 campaign seeds): a contract's count was spent one man for one beast, so a job whose ground dealt dire wolves read 0.1 to 0.2 where the same count of men read 0.7 to 0.9, and a hunt asked a fixed 4, 7 or 10 kills (its row's own 7 for the wolves at the water) whatever the company: a new crew of three met nine dire wolves on a three-skull hunt and lost every one. NOW (slices/bohemia_job_kinds.js __THE_CONTRACT_IS_THE_BUDGET__): beast_cost[kind] is how many of that beast stand for one man of the contract's count (a kind not here stands one for one; the fight's own count_scale for the kinds it already thins is not doubled: no kind is in both, a gate holds it); a hunt's pack is the contract's count at that cost (the flat four fifths for the others); hunt_scales: a hunt's kills grow and shrink with the company the way the contract's count does, in that beast's cost. Draft: TUNING owns the numbers and moves them.

measured.crew: newcrew (three men, level 2, its own kit)

job_contract.pack_flat_why: the flat four fifths a hunt's pack was before (WORLD's 'a beast fights harder than a man, so a pack is four fifths of a crew job's count'), moved out of the code into this file: a beast the table does not cost keeps it, and a costed beast's kills are asked in its cost over this
job_contract.split_why: JOBS 11/10 (rule 443(c)): Battle Brothers' contract type carries the whole job in one base value (bb_all/0827), so a job of N same fights (a defence's waves, a caravan's raids, a patrol's bands) splits one contract: each fight is this share of the contract's count (one fight keeps the whole; two 0.65 each, 1.3 in all; three 0.5 each, 1.5 in all: more fights stay a bigger job, never two or three jobs). MEASURED before (the 11/10d survey): each wave took the whole count and a new crew of three lost 19 in 100 of its defences; the after is in records/BOHEMIA_JOBS_MORE_CONTRACT_KINDS_THE_BATTLE_BROTHERS_WAY_11_10_26.md
